meta.title: stm32/eth: Improve Ethernet driver with link detection and static IP support.
meta.body_summary: Improve STM32 Ethernet driver with automatic cable link detection, static IP before activation, non-blocking PHY, DHCP timing fixes, and network initialization in boot.py, with benchmarked latency improvements.

perf_labels.notes: Claude_Code-driven STM32 Ethernet driver overhaul with link detection, non-blocking PHY, and static IP; merged after detailed code review and community testing confirming correctness.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 529 lines, this is a medium-sized refactor by absolute volume, concentrated in the Ethernet driver (509 lines in eth.c). As a feature/performance PR it merged after a year-long process with multiple review rounds and community testing, reflecting the careful evolution needed for low-level hardware driver changes.

review_details.concern_detail: dpgeorge noted that PHY interrupt register constants in eth_phy.h were unused and questioned the need to change clock-sleep ENABLE to DISABLE in eth_mac_init; Andrew explained the H5 reset timing issue and agreed to add explicit DISABLE with a comment.
review_details.performance_claim: Reduced active() latency from 2s to ~100ms with cable, eliminated 10s timeout without cable, 2x faster network.LAN() instantiation (from ~100ms to ~50ms), and automatic real-time link detection.
review_details.antipattern_addressed: blocking_phy_autonegotiation (prior behavior; not in taxonomy enum)

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: The PR involved deep embedded networking expertise (PHY, LWIP, STM32 HAL). Claude_Code succeeded by providing detailed benchmark data, comprehensive commit messages, and engaging with a community tester who validated the fix; maintainers focused on code cleanup and design consistency.

detection_detail.code_reading: dpgeorge reviewed the diff for unused constants and clock-sleep configuration, leading to discussion about H5 reset requirements.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: PR includes benchmark table with before/after times, and community member panuph independently reproduced and confirmed the behavioral fixes with detailed test output.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: Review comments prompted removal of unused PHY interrupt register defines and refinement of clock-sleep handling; all feedback addressed within the PR.

core_change_summary.description: In ports/stm32/eth.c, added PHY link polling in ETH_IRQHandler, early netif registration for static IP before active(), moved PHY init from mac_init to eth_start, and removed blocking autonegotiation loops; in ports/stm32/main.c, moved mod_network_init() before boot.py for early network interface creation.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Minor adjustments to headers and the network LAN module to support new interface state management.
change_trajectory: Commit 1 (bfe67947): Add link state detection and fix active() method - 51 lines across 4 files.
Commit 2 (cb3833e9): Permanently register netif with lwip - 242 lines in eth.c (main restructuring).
Commit 3 (15390339): Optimize PHY lifecycle and status management - 225 lines across eth.c, eth.h, mpnetworkport.c.
Commit 4 (47bace56): Move network init before boot.py - 11 lines in main.c and mpnetworkport.c.

review_signals.summary: PHY interrupt register constants in eth_phy.h are not used anywhere.
review_signals.action_taken: Andrew acknowledged and noted that interrupts are not feasible due to pin sharing; constants likely removed or kept as documentation.

review_signals.summary: Questioned the necessity of changing __HAL_RCC_ETH_CLK_SLEEP_ENABLE to DISABLE.
review_signals.action_taken: Andrew explained H5 reset timing issue; dpgeorge later agreed it's OK to disable clock-sleep and asked to add a comment.

review_signals.summary: Confirmed that disabling clock-sleep prevents WFI-induced reset timeouts when cable is connected.
review_signals.action_taken: Planned to add explicit DISABLE with explanatory comment.

review_signals.summary: Will test and add explicit DISABLE with comment for clarity.
Provided detailed before/after test output showing isconnected() works correctly and ETIMEDOUT is no longer raised.
